strategies.overview: With its impressive stats, versatile movepool, good typing, and notable ability, Piloswine cements itself as one of the premier staples of the metagame. All these traits allow it to function as an excellent wallbreaker, entry hazard setter, revenge killer, and Thunder Wave absorber. As a hazard setter, being unsusceptible to Taunt owing to its ability is a major plus point. While Eviolite provides bulk and flexibility, Choice Band enables Piloswine to capitalize on its unresisted STAB combination to dismantle opposing teams. However, despite its strength and bulk, it lacks longevity due to the absence of non-Rest recovery moves and faces competition from other Stealth Rock setters like Tinkatuff and Dunsparce, which have relatively better longevity, better matchup against the tier's premier hazard removal option in Quaxwell, and greater overall utility.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Trailblaze over Ice Shard or Stealth Rock with more Speed EVs is an option for Piloswine. For instance, it outspeeds Frogadier at +2 with 104 Speed EVs. Trailblaze transforms Piloswine into a good late-game cleaner, potentially bypassing checks like Thwackey at low HP and picking off foes like Monferno. This alternative also helps it in winning mirror matchups. However, if one drops Stealth Rock, it's advisable to run another setter like Tinkatuff, or if one drops Ice Shard, consider other revenge killers like Thwackey and Choice Scarf Frogadier. Similarly, Curse is an option over Stealth Rock, making Piloswine a dangerous late-game cleaner and enabling it to beat its former checks such as Thwackey and Raboot.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Quaxwell can switch into any move from Piloswine and use Rapid Spin to remove Stealth Rock. It can do so multiple times thanks to Roost and threatens Piloswine out with its STAB moves. Other Water-types like Wartortle and Frogadier can check Piloswine with their STAB attacks too. Wartortle also has Rapid Spin to remove Stealth Rock and is bulky enough to switch into Piloswine once or twice; Frogadier is relatively frailer but stronger.

Wallbreakers and Revenge Killers: Thwackey can check Piloswine, but it usually needs support to get Piloswine weakened to Grassy Glide range, generally with Knock Off, strong super effective moves, or pivoting moves, as it would rather not risk Wood Hammer. Raboot, Monferno, and Pignite heavily damage Piloswine with their Fighting-type moves. Pokemon such as Choice Specs Girafarig, Servine, and Pawniard do a decent job in picking Piloswine off.

Dunsparce: Dunsparce is physically bulky enough to easily take all of Piloswine's STAB moves with impunity. Dunsparce cripples Piloswine with Toxic and can recover the damage off with Roost.

movesets.name: Offensive Stealth Rock
movesets.description:
Piloswine's strong matchups against the tier's other dominant entry hazard setters, such as Tinkatuff and Koffing, and the tier's premier Defogger, Vullaby, allow it to excel as a highly effective Stealth Rock setter. As a wallbreaker, its unresisted STAB combination is extremely threatening to unprepared teams and those that have been weakened by Knock Off, hazards, or other residual damage. High Horsepower allows Piloswine to work effectively even in Grassy Terrain, but Earthquake is also a viable alternative due to its extra power and accuracy. Ice Shard allows Piloswine to pick off weakened threats like Girafarig and Fraxure.

Piloswine is a strong fit for most archetypes, and it's especially effective on bulky offense and balance teams. Drakloak is a good teammate for Piloswine; its spinblocking ability, which allows it to handle Quaxwell, complements Piloswine's Stealth Rock setting perfectly. In addition, Drakloak can spread status to support Piloswine's wallbreaking or work in tandem with it to dismantle the opposing team through pivoting. Frogadier is also a superb partner, forming an entry hazard-stacking core with Piloswine; moreover, it provides pivoting support to Piloswine, creating valuable entry opportunities. In a similar vein, Koffing sets Toxic Spikes to maximize hazard pressure; it also acts as a great switch-in to many foes that Piloswine is weak to, handling Grass-types like Thwackey and Servine and absorbing Fighting-type moves from threats like Raboot, Monferno, and Pignite. In general, wallbreakers and cleaners appreciate Piloswine's Stealth Rock support and offensive pressure; Thwackey, Girafarig, Fraxure, and Raboot synergize extremely well with Piloswine, working hand in hand with it to dismantle defensive cores, which may include Pokemon like Dunsparce, Ivysaur, Quaxwell, and Koffing. Thwackey, in particular, is an excellent teammate for Piloswine, dealing with pesky Water-types that check Piloswine, namely Quaxwell, Wartortle, and Frogadier. Thwackey also offers invaluable Knock Off, pivoting, and passive recovery support, bolstering Piloswine's wallbreaking prowess and longevity. In return, Piloswine deals with foes that can prove to be problematic for Thwackey, such as Koffing, Vullaby, and Tinkatuff. Piloswine appreciates Knock Off support a ton; thus, Knock Off users such as Monferno, Pignite, and Ivysaur make amazing teammates, pairing nicely with Piloswine and amplifying its offensive pressure, even allowing it to reach thresholds like 2HKOing maximum Defense Quaxwell that has lost its Eviolite with minimum chip damage. Defensively, Quaxwell is a remarkable teammate, providing Rapid Spin support to ensure Piloswine's side of the field is free of hazards, thus maximizing hazard pressure on the opposing team. Quaxwell also acts as a switch-in to multiple Pokemon that Piloswine can struggle against, especially if it's chipped or if its Eviolite has been removed by Knock Off, such as Frogadier, Pignite, Monferno, and Raboot; in exchange, Piloswine can deal with foes that Quaxwell is weak to, like Drakloak, Fraxure, and Girafarig. Wartortle is also a good teammate in this regard, though it has less longevity, which is a fair trade for the added offensive pressure. Ivysaur defensively takes care of Grass- and Water-types like Thwackey and Quaxwell for Piloswine, while Piloswine takes care of threats like Girafarig and Tinkatuff.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Thanks to its insane Attack and amazing movepool, Choice Band Piloswine is one of the deadliest wallbreakers and revenge killers of the metagame. High Horsepower is the preferred move under Thwackey's Grassy Terrain, while Earthquake serves as a more consistent option outside of it. Ice Shard picks off foes like Fraxure, Gabite, and low-HP Girafarig. 124 Speed EVs ensure Piloswine outspeeds Quaxwell without Speed investment. Maximum Attack and Speed investment can also be used to not risk Speed tier shenanigans.

Piloswine fits on bulky offense and balance teams. It is best paired with entry hazard setters like Tinkatuff, Frogadier, and Koffing to relentlessly pressure foes like Quaxwell and wallbreak as effectively as possible. Tinkatuff and Koffing also act as Knock Off absorbers, aiding Piloswine in keeping its Choice Band, and they also check Grass-types like Thwackey, Ivysaur, and Servine. Tinkatuff can also try to steal Quaxwell's Eviolite with Pickpocket, invalidating it as a potential Piloswine answer. Monferno and Pignite provide Knock Off support and offensively pressure Quaxwell structures Piloswine may face some difficulty against. Special stallbreakers and wallbreakers such as Servine and Choice Specs Girafarig can work in tandem with Piloswine to dismantle opposing defensive cores with Pokemon like Quaxwell, Dunsparce, Ivysaur, and Tinkatuff. Thwackey and Ivysaur check pesky Water-types that check Piloswine, namely Frogadier, Wartortle, and Quaxwell, while also providing Knock Off support and, in Thwackey's case, passive recovery. In return, Piloswine handles Tinkatuff and Vullaby for them. Piloswine likes taking as little chip damage as possible, so hazard control options such as Quaxwell, Wartortle, and Vullaby are appreciated. Fraxure can take advantage of the holes Piloswine blows into opposing teams to set up and sweep. Servine is also an excellent partner for similar reasons and aids Piloswine by checking Water-types and providing Glare support, potentially mitigating its issue of having mediocre Speed. Pikachu also checks Water-types and provides Volt Switch support to Piloswine, bringing it in on forced switches and enabling its wallbreaking.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 7 onwards

Price Range: 2-3 points

Overview: Piloswine functions quite well in Draft as a low-budget Ground-type and Stealth Rock user that packs a punch early-game. Piloswine also has two very useful abilities. With the ability Oblivious, it can set Stealth Rock reliably without fear of Taunt. Alternatively, Piloswine can also utilize its ability Thick Fat to neutralize its weakness to Fire and grant it a resistance to Ice. The biggest draw to Piloswine, however, is its ability to run Eviolite, boosting its defenses in combination with its already high HP stat. This, combined with Piloswine's relatively strong Attack stat, threatening dual STAB combination, and ability to use priority moves, makes this wooly pig a unique lower tier draft option.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Entry Hazard Setter: Piloswine's bread and butter. Typically always running Stealth Rock, Earthquake, and Ice Shard for priority, Piloswine is quite reliable at showing up early-game, even potentially as a dedicated lead, setting up Stealth Rocks, sponging a few early hits due to its Eviolite-boosted bulk, and getting a few strong Earthquakes off before going down. The real potential for innovation in this common Piloswine variant comes in the 4th moveslot.

Priority Revenge Killer: Piloswine's powerful Ice Shard alone grants it the ability to revenge kill some of Draft's most powerful but Ice-weak Pokemon. Holding Piloswine in the back prevents Pokemon such as Garchomp and Dragonite from sweeping. Piloswine variants with this role will likely run maximum Attack investment and have the potential to clean entire games with Ice Shard if the opposing team is worn down enough.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Earthquake, Icicle Crash, Ice Shard

Setup Moves: Curse

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Roar

Coverage: Rock Slide, Stone Edge, Throat Chop

Niche Moves

Endeavor: After sponging a few hits, Piloswine can use its low health to its advantage by clicking Endeavor against bulkier foes.

Freeze-Dry: Even though Piloswine's Special Attack stat is low, Freeze-Dry can be a niche choice for coverage against Pelipper and Gyarados, both of which are 4x weak to the move.

High Horsepower: A niche alternative if either team has a Grassy Surge user, which would weaken Earthquake but not High Horsepower.

Common Items

Eviolite: Piloswine should nearly always hold Eviolite. The ability to significantly boost Piloswine's defenses massively outweighs any value any other item could give.

Niche Items

Custap Berry: In very niche hyper offensive builds after Piloswine has set Stealth Rock, Piloswine can use Endure paired with a Custap Berry to click a priority powerful STAB move before going down.

Tera

Piloswine has very little reason to Terastallize; its base Ground-type makes it a useful Electric-immune teamslot, and there are far better low-tier options regardless. However, if Piloswine is to Terastallize, then Tera Grass paired with Thick Fat can be a strong defensive option while also giving Piloswine the ability to hit Water-types for super-effective damage with Tera Blast. Otherwise, Tera Ghost can be useful to block Rapid Spin.

Draft Strategy

Piloswine is useful on drafts that seek entry hazards to support powerful wallbreakers or setup sweepers. It also has value as a Ground-type, a must-have typing in Draft thanks to its Electric immunity. Piloswine also has value on drafts that otherwise lack reliable forms of priority. Piloswine should primarily be used as an early-game piece, so it functions well on teams that have a lot of other wincons.

Wallbreakers and Sweepers: The Stealth Rock that Piloswine sets up is useful for powerful wallbreakers such as Chi-Yu and Iron Valiant to secure certain OHKOs or 2HKOs after entry hazard damage. These wallbreakers may also put foes in Ice Shard KO range for Piloswine. Entry hazard damage also helps setup sweepers such as Quaquaval and Ogerpon-W sweep easier.

Rapid Spin: Spinners such as Terapagos and Blastoise are good support options to pair with Piloswine so that entry hazards can be removed while keeping Piloswine's Stealth Rock on the field. Piloswine also appreciates having hazards removed for its own defensive capabilities, since it never uses Heavy-Duty Boots and lacks access to recovery.

Offensive Ground-types: Piloswine is unlike other Ground-types in that its Thick Fat ability and secondary typing effectively give it a resistance to Ice. Thus, Piloswine can be safely paired with other offensive Ground-types like Garchomp and Landorus without fear of stacking weaknesses. This takes the pressure of setting Stealth Rock off of other offensive Ground-types and frees them up to be all-out attackers or setup sweepers.

Checks and Counters

Status: A burned Piloswine is a very sad Piloswine. The residual chip and Attack drop from burn greatly diminish Piloswine's main draw as a tanky sponge with offensive potential. Toxic also will gradually wear down its unrecoverable HP.

Knock Off: Knocking off Piloswine's Eviolite will greatly reduce its ability to tank a subsequent hit. Any strong, super effective hit afterwards will likely take it out.

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Slowking and Milotic resist Piloswine's Ice STAB moves, tank Earthquake with relative ease, and threaten it back with Scald. Rotom-W is also one of the best counters to Piloswine, as it is immune to Piloswine's Earthquake and can threaten it with Hydro Pump or a burn.

Powerful Special Attackers: Piloswine is much weaker on its special side, so even with Eviolite, it struggles to chew more than one hit from Water-types like Manaphy and Primarina and even prominent special attacking Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Archaludon.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive Wall (Ice)
movesets.description: Piloswine is one of Ice teams' best specially defensive walls, capable of filling some of Ice teams' biggest roles of being an entry hazard setter and Electric immunity. Thick Fat coupled with Eviolite gives Piloswine tremendous bulk, with which it can check dangerous Fire-type threats to Ice such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y by disposing of them with Rock Slide. 12 EVs in Attack guarantees an OHKO on offensive Volcarona. Another one of Piloswine's amazing traits is its Ground typing, which makes it a great asset in the Electric matchup by preventing a Volt Switch onslaught while also letting it hit Electric-types super effectively with STAB Earthquake. Toxic is an option to put defensive switch-ins such as Skeledirge and Rotom-W on a timer, helping Piloswine's teammates overpower them, but Roar is an alternative choice to force out threats that may use it to set up, such as Mega Scizor, and to rack up hazard damage from its Stealth Rock and Cloyster's Spikes to wear down threats such as Urshifu-R and Mega Venusaur. Piloswine appreciates Alolan Ninetales's snow and Aurora Veil, which let it wall the opposition more easily. Piloswine is, however, extremely vulnerable to Water-types, so partnering it with Kyurem or Arctozolt is appreciated, as they can easily break Water teams. Substitute Baxcalibur also threatens Poison teams, which can cripple Piloswine with Toxic. Weavile with a Z-Crystal is also a good Knock Off absorber for Piloswine, as losing Eviolite ruins Piloswine; Weavile also forces immense progress by removing key items from Celesteela and Skeledirge, which become susceptible to Stealth Rock afterwards, or outright breaking through them with a Z-Move. Galarian Darmanitan and Shell Smash Cloyster can threaten Steel teams with Flare Blitz and Hydro Pump or Hidden Power Fire, respectively. The Stealth Rocks and Toxic spread by Piloswine also accentuates the breaking power of teammates such as Swords Dance or Dragon Dance Baxcalibur and Belly Drum Cetitan. IronPress Avalugg and defensive Cloyster with Hidden Power Fire are also good partners in being able to shut down Mega Scizor. Avalugg, Articuno, and Cloyster are also capable of removing entry hazards, with the latter two also being able to pivot in Piloswine with U-turn and Teleport, respectively.
